tech.name: FINA 101 · Principles of Finance
tech.description: Prices a bond, a loan, and a retirement plan with the time value of money, then asks why risk raises what investors demand.

tech.name: FINA 110 · Corporate Finance
tech.description: Decides which projects a firm should fund and how to pay for them. The cost of capital is the bar every project has to clear.

tech.name: FINA 120 · Investment Analysis
tech.description: Assembles a portfolio of stocks and bonds on the trade-off between risk and return, and tests whether the market priced any of it correctly.

tech.name: FINA 130 · Real Estate Finance
tech.description: Values property and the mortgages written against it, starting with a single rental and ending with a securitized pool of loans.

tech.name: FINA 140 · International Finance
tech.description: Hedges a firm that earns in one currency and owes in another, and learns how capital is raised and moved across borders.

tech.name: FINA 210 · Financial Modeling
tech.description: Builds three-statement, discounted cash flow, and scenario models in spreadsheets, with the sensitivity tests that show where a valuation breaks.

tech.name: FINA 220 · Fintech & Blockchain
tech.description: Takes apart payments apps, lending platforms, and distributed ledgers to see which of them changes finance and which only re-plumbs it.

tech.name: FINA 230 · Risk Management
tech.description: Measures market, credit, and operational risk with value-at-risk and stress tests. What to hedge with derivatives and what to insure is the judgment call.

tech.name: FINA 240 · Behavioral Finance
tech.description: Works out how loss aversion and herding push prices away from what rational models predict, and why arbitrage so often fails to push them back.

tech.name: FINA 310 · Senior Seminar in Finance
tech.description: Takes one live deal to an investment committee's vote, defending the valuation, the financing, and the risks before a panel of practitioners.

tech.name: ACCT 101 · Introduction to Accounting
tech.description: Records a small firm's first year in journal entries and closes it into a balance sheet and an income statement.

tech.name: ACCT 110 · Financial Accounting
tech.description: Prepares and reads the balance sheet, income statement, and cash-flow statement under the standards that govern external reporting.

tech.name: ACCT 120 · Managerial Accounting
tech.description: Turns cost data into budgets, break-even points, variance reports, and prices for the people who run the business.

tech.name: ACCT 130 · Tax Fundamentals
tech.description: Computes the tax owed by a household and by a small business, then reruns their decisions to see what the code rewards.

tech.name: ACCT 140 · Accounting Information Systems
tech.description: Tracks a transaction through enterprise software, past each control built into its path, to the places where the controls fail.

tech.name: ACCT 210 · Forensic Accounting
tech.description: Follows money through fraud schemes, asset tracing, and litigation support, using the accounting record as evidence.

tech.name: ACCT 220 · Intermediate Financial Reporting
tech.description: Handles the hard cases in external reporting: revenue recognition, leases, pensions, and income taxes. Consolidations are saved for last.

tech.name: ACCT 230 · Cost Accounting
tech.description: Every costing system distorts something. Activity-based costing and transfer prices are studied for what they do to the performance measures built on them.

tech.name: ACCT 240 · Auditing Principles
tech.description: Gathers evidence and tests internal controls as an auditor would, to decide whether a company's financial statements can be relied on.

tech.name: ACCT 310 · Senior Seminar in Accounting
tech.description: Works a full engagement for a mid-sized company: closing its books, preparing its tax return, and testing its statements. Every judgment call gets written up.

tech.name: MRKT 101 · Fundamentals of Marketing
tech.description: Takes a brand apart into product, price, place, and promotion, one case at a time.

tech.name: MRKT 110 · Consumer Behavior
tech.description: Draws on psychology and economics to explain how people notice, evaluate, and choose products. Quite often, habit and context have chosen for them.

tech.name: MRKT 120 · Market Research
tech.description: Asks customers what they want by survey and focus group, then runs the experiment that shows what they do.

tech.name: MRKT 130 · Digital Marketing Strategy
tech.description: Plans search, social, email, and paid campaigns around the funnel. Each is measured by what it sold, not by how many people scrolled past it.

tech.name: MRKT 140 · Brand Management
tech.description: Builds and defends a brand as an asset: positioning, identity, extensions, and the valuation of what the name alone is worth.

tech.name: MRKT 210 · Sports Marketing
tech.description: Markets teams and leagues through sponsorship and media rights, a business whose product changes with every game.

tech.name: MRKT 220 · Advertising & Promotion
tech.description: Writes the creative brief and the media plan for a campaign, and judges it against the behavior it set out to change.

tech.name: MRKT 230 · Sales Management
tech.description: Draws territories and sets quotas and commissions for a sales force. The rest is forecasting the pipeline and coaching the team to close more of it.

tech.name: MRKT 240 · Global Marketing
tech.description: Carries one product across cultures, currencies, and regulators. The standing question is what to standardize and what to localize.

tech.name: MRKT 310 · Capstone: Marketing Strategy
tech.description: Plans a year of marketing for an outside client, from the research to the budget. The client's managers attend the final presentation and bring their own questions.

tech.name: Experimental Economics Lab
tech.description: Behavioral labs and market-simulation suites. The Economics program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: ECON 101 · Microeconomics
tech.description: Works out what households and firms choose when they cannot have everything, with supply and demand first and market structure after.

tech.name: ECON 110 · Macroeconomics
tech.description: Models output, unemployment, inflation, and growth for a whole economy. What a central bank or a budget can do about any of them is the open question.

tech.name: ECON 120 · Econometrics
tech.description: Fits regression lines to economic data and tests whether a correlation, however strong, can be read as a cause.

tech.name: ECON 130 · Intermediate Microeconomics
tech.description: Reworks consumer choice, the firm, and market failure with the calculus the principles course left out. What that course could only assert, this one derives.

tech.name: ECON 140 · Economic History
tech.description: Reads the Industrial Revolution, the Great Depression, and the postwar boom as tests of economic theory rather than as a chronicle.

tech.name: ECON 210 · Behavioral Economics
tech.description: Replaces the rational agent with the one experiments find, and works out what bounded rationality and present bias do to markets and policy.

tech.name: ECON 220 · Public Finance
tech.description: Asks who bears a tax, what a public good is worth, and when redistribution costs efficiency. The answers decide what to make of public spending and debt.

tech.name: ECON 230 · Game Theory
tech.description: Finds the Nash equilibrium of an auction or an arms race, where the best move depends on what everyone else is about to do.

tech.name: ECON 240 · Environmental Economics
tech.description: Prices pollution, climate damage, and natural resources, then ranks taxes, tradable permits, and regulation by cost per ton of emissions cut.

tech.name: ECON 310 · Senior Seminar in Economics
tech.description: Writes an empirical paper on a question of the student's own, and defends the data and the identification before a seminar that has read it.

tech.name: MGMT 101 · Organizational Leadership
tech.description: Learns what a first-time manager can do when a team forms, stalls, or recovers. The term's team projects supply fresh examples of all three.

tech.name: MGMT 110 · Human Resources Management
tech.description: Treats pay and performance review as the levers that decide who stays at a firm, with recruiting and employment law on either side.

tech.name: MGMT 120 · Operations Management
tech.description: Finds the bottleneck. However its capacity and schedule are planned, the slowest step sets what a process can make and deliver.

tech.name: MGMT 130 · Business Ethics
tech.description: Tests corporate decisions against moral frameworks, stakeholder claims, and the cases where the law permitted what the public would not.

tech.name: MGMT 140 · Organizational Behavior
tech.description: Applies research on motivation, perception, and group decisions to why people at work cooperate, quit, or go along with a bad call.

tech.name: MGMT 210 · Project Management
tech.description: Plans scope, schedule, budget, and risk with work breakdowns and critical paths. Then the project starts, and the plans meet reality.

tech.name: MGMT 220 · Entrepreneurship
tech.description: Takes one idea from the first customer interview to a funded launch, and learns how ventures fail at each stage in between.

tech.name: MGMT 230 · Conflict Resolution
tech.description: Diagnoses a workplace dispute before trying to settle it. Mediation and interest-based bargaining fix different problems, and the wrong one makes things worse.

tech.name: MGMT 240 · Negotiations
tech.description: Negotiates in live simulations every week, starting with a haggle over price and ending with multi-party deals where interests are hidden.

tech.name: MGMT 310 · Strategic Management
tech.description: Brings finance, marketing, and operations together in full company cases, starting with the five forces. A strategy passes only if it holds once rivals respond.

tech.name: SPCO 101 · Introduction to Supply Chain
tech.description: Traces how goods move from raw material to customer, and where supply chains break down.

tech.name: SPCO 110 · Logistics & Distribution
tech.description: Plans where to keep goods and how to ship them, trading inventory against speed and cost.

tech.name: SPCO 120 · Procurement & Sourcing
tech.description: Chooses suppliers and negotiates their contracts, on the understanding that the lowest price is rarely the lowest cost.

tech.name: SPCO 130 · Quality Management
tech.description: Applies statistical process control, Six Sigma, and root-cause analysis to keep defects out of a product before inspection finds them.

tech.name: SPCO 140 · Demand Planning
tech.description: Forecasts what customers will order from past sales, promotions, and market signals. Every forecast is wrong, so the craft is in being wrong by less and telling operations early.

tech.name: SPCO 210 · Global Supply Chains
tech.description: Stretches a supply chain across borders, where tariffs and currency move the cost and a closed port can stop everything.

tech.name: SPCO 220 · Inventory Control Systems
tech.description: Decides when to reorder and how much safety stock to hold, for demand that is uncertain and lead times that slip.

tech.name: SPCO 230 · Data Analytics for Operations
tech.description: Fits optimization, simulation, and forecasting models to routing, scheduling, and stock decisions, using a company's own operating data.

tech.name: SPCO 240 · Transportation Management
tech.description: Moves freight by road, rail, sea, and air: choosing carriers, routing fleets, and writing contracts as regulation and fuel prices shift.

tech.name: SPCO 310 · Capstone: Supply Chain Design
tech.description: Redesigns a partner company's supply chain as a team, modeling its network, inventory, and costs. Its managers get the savings estimate and ask the first hard questions.

tech.name: Mechanical Engineering Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Mechanical Engineering program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: MECH 101 · Introduction to Mechanical Design
tech.description: Sketches freehand, models in CAD, and reads an engineering drawing. Each team then builds a prototype that has to meet a written specification.

tech.name: MECH 110 · Statics & Dynamics
tech.description: Analyzes forces and moments on trusses, frames, and machines at rest, then on particles and rigid bodies under acceleration.

tech.name: MECH 120 · Thermodynamics
tech.description: Runs engines and refrigerators through the first and second laws with a book of property tables, and accepts the efficiency the second law allows.

tech.name: MECH 130 · Fluid Mechanics
tech.description: Follows a fluid through pipes and around bodies, from Bernoulli and the Navier-Stokes equations to boundary layers and drag.

tech.name: MECH 140 · Materials Science
tech.description: Relates the structure of metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites to their strength, failure, and processing.

tech.name: MECH 210 · Robotics
tech.description: Makes a robot arm and a mobile robot go where they are told, using kinematics to plan the motion and sensors to report how far off it is.

tech.name: MECH 220 · HVAC Systems
tech.description: Sizes the equipment that heats and cools a building from load calculations and psychrometric charts, and checks the result against the energy code.

tech.name: MECH 230 · Internal Combustion Engines
tech.description: Studies how spark- and compression-ignition engines burn fuel and what comes out the tailpipe. The lab has a running engine on a dynamometer, waiting to be tuned.

tech.name: MECH 240 · Finite Element Analysis
tech.description: Solves stress, thermal, and vibration problems numerically. A converged result can still be wrong, and telling when is most of the skill.

tech.name: MECH 310 · Mechanical Engineering Senior Design
tech.description: Designs, builds, and tests a working machine for an outside sponsor in a year-long team project, to a budget and a written specification.

tech.name: Electrical Engineering Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Electrical Engineering program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: ELEC 101 · Circuits
tech.description: Solves resistive, RC, and RL circuits with Kirchhoff's laws, nodal analysis, and Thévenin equivalents. Each answer gets checked on a breadboard.

tech.name: ELEC 110 · Digital Logic Design
tech.description: Designs combinational and sequential circuits from gates and flip-flops, and builds them on programmable hardware.

tech.name: ELEC 120 · Signals & Systems
tech.description: Moves signals into the frequency domain with Fourier, Laplace, and z-transforms, where the linear systems that filter them become easy to read.

tech.name: ELEC 130 · Electromagnetics
tech.description: Develops Maxwell's equations for static fields and then for waves, until antennas and transmission lines stop being mysterious.

tech.name: ELEC 140 · Microelectronics
tech.description: Analyzes and designs diode and transistor circuits with small-signal models, and biases amplifiers to tolerate temperature drift and part-to-part variation.

tech.name: ELEC 210 · Power Systems Analysis
tech.description: Models generation, transmission, and load flow in the electrical grid, with fault analysis and the stability of the network.

tech.name: ELEC 220 · Wireless Communications
tech.description: Sends bits over a fading channel with modulation and coding, and works out the link budget that decides whether a call connects.

tech.name: ELEC 230 · Control Systems
tech.description: Designs feedback controllers with root locus, frequency response, and state space. Tuning happens on lab hardware, which has not read the model.

tech.name: ELEC 240 · VLSI Design
tech.description: Lays out digital circuits in CMOS one transistor at a time, and closes timing and power before the design goes out to be fabricated.

tech.name: ELEC 310 · Electrical Engineering Senior Design
tech.description: Takes a team's circuit board or embedded system through specification, prototype, and test. On the last day it has to work in front of a review panel.

tech.name: Chemical Engineering Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Chemical Engineering program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: CHEN 101 · Principles of Chemical Engineering
tech.description: Follows a barrel of crude and a vat of corn mash through a plant, and names the unit operation each step takes.

tech.name: CHEN 110 · Chemical Thermodynamics
tech.description: Starts with energy balances on flowing streams, then applies phase and chemical equilibrium to the separations and reactions a plant depends on.

tech.name: CHEN 120 · Fluid Transport
tech.description: Calculates friction losses, pump heads, and pressure drops for process piping, with the Reynolds number deciding which correlation applies.

tech.name: CHEN 130 · Material & Energy Balances
tech.description: Closes mass and energy balances on a whole flowsheet with recycle and purge streams. It is bookkeeping, and every plant design is checked against it.

tech.name: CHEN 140 · Chemical Reaction Engineering
tech.description: Sizes batch, stirred, and tubular reactors from kinetics and residence time, with heat effects and catalysis.

tech.name: CHEN 210 · Process Safety
tech.description: Goes back over the case histories of plant accidents to learn the HAZOP study and the relief system, the tools that let a design fail safely.

tech.name: CHEN 220 · Biochemical Engineering
tech.description: Engineers fermentation, enzyme reactors, and downstream purification to make pharmaceuticals and fuels from living cells.

tech.name: CHEN 230 · Polymer Science
tech.description: Explains why plastics flow like liquids and spring back like solids, starting from how the chains are made and how long they grow.

tech.name: CHEN 240 · Sustainable Energy Technology
tech.description: Evaluates biofuels, hydrogen, carbon capture, and electrochemical storage on efficiency, cost, and life-cycle emissions.

tech.name: CHEN 310 · Chemical Process Design
tech.description: Designs and costs a complete plant as a team, sizing every unit operation and closing the economics that decide whether it would be built.

tech.name: Civil Engineering Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Civil Engineering program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: CIVE 101 · Statics
tech.description: Draws the free-body diagram first. Forces in equilibrium and the path a load takes to the ground follow from it.

tech.name: CIVE 110 · Structural Analysis
tech.description: Finds the force in every member of a determinate truss or frame by statics alone, then rolls a moving load across it with influence lines.

tech.name: CIVE 120 · Soil Mechanics
tech.description: Classifies soil and tests its seepage and shear strength, since the ground decides what a foundation can carry and how far it will settle.

tech.name: CIVE 130 · Mechanics of Materials
tech.description: Relates loads to stress, strain, and deflection in bars, shafts, and beams, up to buckling and combined loading.

tech.name: CIVE 140 · Transportation Engineering
tech.description: Plans roads and transit lines around traffic flow and capacity analysis, by the geometric standards that keep a curve drivable.

tech.name: CIVE 210 · Bridge Design
tech.description: Carries one bridge through the whole term: loads, girders, bearings, and substructure. It ends with the code checks every span has to pass.

tech.name: CIVE 220 · Environmental Impact Assessment
tech.description: Prepares the environmental statement regulators require before a project is built, on what it would do to air and water and to the people nearby.

tech.name: CIVE 230 · Construction Management
tech.description: Plans a construction project through its estimate, schedule, contracts, and safety program, on a site that has weather and subcontractors.

tech.name: CIVE 240 · Urban Planning
tech.description: Drafts a comprehensive plan for how a town zones its land and houses its people. The plan then has to survive a public hearing.

tech.name: CIVE 310 · Civil Engineering Senior Design
tech.description: Acts as a consulting team on an actual site, designing its structures, drainage, and roads to code. The drawings and cost estimate go to a client to sign.

tech.name: INDE 101 · Introduction to Industrial Systems
tech.description: Maps a process, times its jobs with a stopwatch, and puts a dollar figure on each proposed improvement.

tech.name: INDE 110 · Production Planning
tech.description: Schedules materials, machines, and people to meet demand, with MRP, capacity planning, and the trade-off between inventory and lead time.

tech.name: INDE 120 · Ergonomics & Safety
tech.description: Fits the workstation, the tool, and the task to the human body, since the reverse does not work. Hazard analysis covers what is left.

tech.name: INDE 130 · Quality Control
tech.description: Watches a process on control charts to catch drift before it becomes defects, and samples what the charts cannot see.

tech.name: INDE 140 · Facilities Design
tech.description: Lays out plants and warehouses for material flow, with location analysis and the space each operation needs.

tech.name: INDE 210 · Simulation Modeling
tech.description: Builds discrete-event models of factories, hospitals, and queues, for running the experiments nobody could afford to run on the originals.

tech.name: INDE 220 · Supply Chain Analytics
tech.description: Optimizes a working supply chain with mathematical programming, deciding where to source and how much to stock.

tech.name: INDE 230 · Lean Manufacturing
tech.description: Strips the waste out of a production line with value-stream maps and pull systems, then does it again, because the improvement is meant to be continuous.

tech.name: INDE 240 · Reliability Engineering
tech.description: Models failure with life distributions and fault trees, and designs maintenance and redundancy for systems that must not stop.

tech.name: INDE 310 · Industrial Engineering Senior Design
tech.description: Spends the term inside a partner plant or hospital, modeling how its work flows. The proposal has to say what each change costs and what waiting it removes.

tech.name: Aerospace Engineering Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Aerospace Engineering program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: AERO 101 · Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
tech.description: Learns what keeps an aircraft up and a satellite in orbit, starting with the standard atmosphere and the airfoil.

tech.name: AERO 110 · Aerodynamics
tech.description: Predicts lift and drag on airfoils and wings with potential-flow theory and compressibility corrections, and tests the predictions in a wind tunnel.

tech.name: AERO 120 · Aircraft Performance
tech.description: Computes range, endurance, climb, and takeoff and landing distances from an aircraft's thrust, drag, and weight.

tech.name: AERO 130 · Spacecraft Propulsion
tech.description: Lives by the rocket equation. It sets how much propellant any mission must carry, whether the engine is a chemical rocket or an electric thruster.

tech.name: AERO 140 · Aerospace Structures
tech.description: Analyzes thin-walled beams, stressed skins, and composites under flight loads, with fatigue and the margins certification demands.

tech.name: AERO 210 · Astrodynamics
tech.description: Solves two-body orbits, transfers, and rendezvous. The final problem is a trajectory to another planet, with gravity assists doing some of the work.

tech.name: AERO 220 · Rocketry
tech.description: Flies a sounding rocket the team designed and built. Afterward the team answers for its motor choice, its stability margin, and where the rocket came down.

tech.name: AERO 230 · Aircraft Design
tech.description: Turns a mission requirement into an aircraft on paper, one trade study at a time, until it can face a preliminary design review.

tech.name: AERO 240 · Unmanned Aerial Systems
tech.description: Builds a drone from airframe, autopilot, and sensors. It flies only where and as high as the FAA allows.

tech.name: AERO 310 · Aerospace Senior Design
tech.description: Designs an aircraft or a spacecraft mission as a team and defends it at a design review. The weight budget is usually the last to close.

tech.name: MDIA 101 · Mass Communication
tech.description: Counts what newspapers, broadcasters, and platforms each reach. What they do to opinion is a harder question, and the research on it is read with care.

tech.name: MDIA 110 · Media Theory
tech.description: Reads the major theories of media effects and meaning, from propaganda models to audience reception, against what the evidence supports.

tech.name: MDIA 120 · Global Media Systems
tech.description: Compares countries by who owns the press and who pays for the broadcasters. Each arrangement produces recognizably different news.

tech.name: MDIA 130 · Digital Culture
tech.description: Asks what platforms and their algorithms have done to identity and to the public sphere, now that the audience also publishes.

tech.name: MDIA 140 · Media Ethics
tech.description: Works through privacy, deception, harm, and conflict of interest in journalism and entertainment, case by case.

tech.name: MDIA 210 · Film Industry
tech.description: Tracks a film from development finance through distribution windows and marketing, and learns how streaming rewrote the economics.

tech.name: MDIA 220 · Social Media Analytics
tech.description: Measures reach, sentiment, and network spread across platforms. The work is separating an audience from bots and vanity metrics.

tech.name: MDIA 230 · Photojournalism
tech.description: Shoots, edits, and captions news photographs under deadline, with the ethics of staging, cropping, and consent.

tech.name: MDIA 240 · Public Relations
tech.description: Looks after an organization's reputation with the press on good days and in a crisis, and measures afterward what the coverage did.

tech.name: MDIA 310 · Senior Seminar in Media Studies
tech.description: Researches one medium, company, or audience through archives, interviews, or data. The thesis that results is defended before the seminar.

tech.name: GRDS 101 · Visual Communication
tech.description: Composes shape, color, and type on posters and signs. The test is whether a viewer sees first what the designer meant them to.

tech.name: GRDS 110 · Typography
tech.description: Sets type from a single word mark to a page of running text, with close attention to letterform and spacing. Nobody kerns casually afterward.

tech.name: GRDS 120 · Digital Imaging
tech.description: Edits and composes raster and vector images for print and screen, with color management and resolution handled correctly.

tech.name: GRDS 130 · Layout Design
tech.description: Arranges type and image on the page and the screen using grids, hierarchy, and white space, for editorial and advertising work.

tech.name: GRDS 140 · Branding & Identity
tech.description: Turns a logo into an identity system with written guidelines, and tests it on everything a client will put it on.

tech.name: GRDS 210 · Web Design
tech.description: Lays out responsive interfaces in HTML and CSS that stay navigable and accessible, and tests them on phones slower than the designer's.

tech.name: GRDS 220 · Motion Graphics
tech.description: Animates type and graphics for title sequences, explainers, and broadcast, using timing and easing to carry meaning.

tech.name: GRDS 230 · Illustration
tech.description: Develops a personal visual language through editorial, book, and concept illustration in traditional and digital media.

tech.name: GRDS 240 · Publication Design
tech.description: Designs a complete magazine or book, from pacing and typographic system through the cover to press-ready files.

tech.name: GRDS 310 · Senior Portfolio
tech.description: Refines a professional portfolio around a self-directed identity project, reviewed by practicing designers at a public show.

tech.name: CRWR 101 · Introduction to Creative Writing
tech.description: Writes a poem and a short story a week, read aloud and critiqued, to learn what revision is for.

tech.name: CRWR 110 · Fiction Workshop
tech.description: Drafts and revises short stories under group critique, where the author listens and may not explain what was meant.

tech.name: CRWR 120 · Poetry Workshop
tech.description: Composes poems in received and open forms, revising for image, line, and sound under weekly critique.

tech.name: CRWR 130 · Nonfiction Workshop
tech.description: Tells true stories as memoir, essay, and reportage. Fiction owes nothing to the facts or to the people in it, and this does.

tech.name: CRWR 140 · Literary Editing
tech.description: Edits other writers' manuscripts at the line and the structural level, and produces a small literary magazine from submission to print.

tech.name: CRWR 210 · Screenwriting
tech.description: Writes a feature-length screenplay in industry format, from logline and outline through three-act structure and dialogue.

tech.name: CRWR 220 · Playwriting
tech.description: Develops a one-act play in which everything must be said or done onstage, and hears each draft read aloud by actors.

tech.name: CRWR 230 · Novel Writing
tech.description: Plans and drafts the opening of a novel, sustaining character and plot across a length the short story never asks for.

tech.name: CRWR 240 · Creative Writing Seminar
tech.description: Completes a polished manuscript in the writer's chosen genre, alongside the craft reading and the query letter to send with it.

tech.name: CRWR 310 · Senior Thesis in Creative Writing
tech.description: Gathers a year's poems into a chapbook or its stories into a collection under one faculty reader, and reads from it in public at the end.

tech.name: MUSC 101 · Music Theory I
tech.description: Notates scales and chords by hand until the harmony they make can be heard before it is played.

tech.name: MUSC 110 · Music Theory II
tech.description: Extends harmony into chromaticism, modulation, and form, analyzing sonatas and songs from the score.

tech.name: MUSC 120 · Music History Survey
tech.description: Hears Western art music in order, from chant to Stravinsky, with the scores open. The listening exam can start anywhere in any piece.

tech.name: MUSC 130 · Composition I
tech.description: Writes short pieces for solo instruments and small ensembles, and hears them performed and critiqued.

tech.name: MUSC 140 · Applied Instrument/Voice
tech.description: Takes weekly private lessons on an instrument or in voice, building technique and repertoire toward a performance before a faculty jury.

tech.name: MUSC 210 · Jazz Improvisation
tech.description: Improvises over standards and blues forms, learning chord-scale relationships, voicings, and the vocabulary of the tradition by ear.

tech.name: MUSC 220 · World Music
tech.description: Learns the music of West Africa, India, Indonesia, and the Andes by playing it as well as listening.

tech.name: MUSC 230 · Music Technology
tech.description: Records, mixes, and produces music in a digital audio workstation, with synthesis, sampling, and live electronics.

tech.name: MUSC 240 · Composition II
tech.description: Composes an extended work for larger forces, orchestrated and rehearsed toward a public premiere.

tech.name: MUSC 310 · Senior Recital
tech.description: Prepares and performs a public recital or a portfolio of premiered compositions, with program notes written by the performer.

tech.name: Media Production Studio
tech.description: Sound stages, edit bays and a screening theater. The Film program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: FILM 101 · Introduction to Film Analysis
tech.description: Watches films one shot at a time to see how framing and cutting tell the story.

tech.name: FILM 110 · Cinematography
tech.description: Runs the camera on set: lighting, lenses, exposure, and movement. Each choice changes what an audience feels.

tech.name: FILM 120 · Screenwriting Workshop
tech.description: Takes short scripts to a table read, where dialogue that looked fine on the page is heard for the first time.

tech.name: FILM 130 · Film Production
tech.description: Plans and shoots a short film as a crew, rotating through every job on set so that nobody only directs.

tech.name: FILM 140 · Directing Fundamentals
tech.description: Directs actors and blocks scenes from a script the student has broken into shot lists, with each decision tested on set.

tech.name: FILM 210 · Documentary Filmmaking
tech.description: Researches, shoots, and edits a nonfiction film, negotiating access, consent, and the line between observing and staging.

tech.name: FILM 220 · History of World Cinema
tech.description: Screens the movements that made national cinemas: Soviet montage, Italian neorealism, the French New Wave, and Brazil's Cinema Novo.

tech.name: FILM 230 · Sound Design
tech.description: Records dialogue and builds effects and ambience into a soundtrack that does half the storytelling.

tech.name: FILM 240 · Post-Production
tech.description: Edits, color-grades, and finishes a film to delivery. The file named final is followed by several more.

tech.name: FILM 310 · Thesis Film
tech.description: Directs a short film from the student's own script, with classmates as the crew and the department's festival as the first audience.

tech.name: SART 101 · Fundamentals of 2D Design
tech.description: Arranges line and shape in cut paper and ink until figure and ground balance. The results go up on the wall for critique each week.

tech.name: SART 110 · Drawing
tech.description: Draws from still life and the figure in charcoal and ink, until the hand records what the eye sees and not what the mind expects.

tech.name: SART 120 · Painting
tech.description: Paints in oil and acrylic, first in quick studies of color and surface and then on canvases that take weeks.

tech.name: SART 130 · Sculpture
tech.description: Builds in clay, plaster, wood, and found material. A work that occupies a room has to hold up from every side, including the back.

tech.name: SART 140 · Art History Survey
tech.description: Goes through painting, sculpture, and architecture period by period. The slide exam fades, but the formal analysis is what a studio critique borrows.

tech.name: SART 210 · Printmaking
tech.description: Cuts blocks, etches plates, and pulls screens. In an edition, every sheet has to match the first.

tech.name: SART 220 · Ceramics
tech.description: Throws and hand-builds vessels and sculptural forms, then opens the kiln to find out what the glaze chemistry decided.

tech.name: SART 230 · Photography
tech.description: Shoots, develops, and prints in the darkroom and the digital lab, with the history of the medium alongside the technique.

tech.name: SART 240 · Digital Art
tech.description: Codes generative images and builds 3D models and interactive video, for work that hangs on a screen rather than on paper.

tech.name: SART 310 · Senior Exhibition
tech.description: Makes a coherent body of work over the year, hangs it in the college gallery for public critique, and writes the artist's statement last, under protest.

tech.name: ENGL 101 · Introduction to Literary Studies
tech.description: Reads slowly. Every argument about a poem or a play has to be built from the words on the page.

tech.name: ENGL 110 · British Literature Survey
tech.description: Starts at Beowulf and ends at Woolf, with Chaucer, Milton, and the Romantics between, as English itself changes underfoot.

tech.name: ENGL 120 · American Literature Survey
tech.description: Asks what makes a literature American rather than English, through Bradstreet, Douglass, Dickinson, Twain, Faulkner, and Morrison.

tech.name: ENGL 130 · Critical Theory
tech.description: Puts one text through formalist, Marxist, psychoanalytic, feminist, and postcolonial readings. It comes out different each time.

tech.name: ENGL 140 · Rhetoric & Composition
tech.description: Practices argument and research writing for an academic audience, with sustained revision and attention to style.

tech.name: ENGL 210 · Shakespeare
tech.description: Reads a dozen of the plays across comedy, history, and tragedy, as scripts meant for a stage and as texts whose versions disagree.

tech.name: ENGL 220 · Restoration & 18th Century Literature
tech.description: Keeps company with Swift and Pope through a century of coffeehouses and satire, and is there when the novel arrives.

tech.name: ENGL 230 · Postcolonial Literature
tech.description: Empire left its language behind. The writers of Africa, South Asia, and the Caribbean have answered in it, with a body of theory close behind them.

tech.name: ENGL 240 · Technical Writing
tech.description: Writes instructions and proposals in plain language, then watches a test reader try to follow them. The reader is never wrong.

tech.name: ENGL 310 · Senior Seminar in English
tech.description: Drafts a twenty-five-page critical essay on an author or a problem of the student's choosing, and defends it among peers.

tech.name: SOCY 101 · Introduction to Sociology
tech.description: Finds class, family, school, and work behind choices people believe are their own, using the surveys that measure it.

tech.name: SOCY 110 · Social Stratification
tech.description: Analyzes class, status, and power: how inequality is measured, reproduced across generations, and justified.

tech.name: SOCY 120 · Sociological Theory
tech.description: Sets Marx against Weber and both against Durkheim, asking what each framework explains that the others cannot.

tech.name: SOCY 130 · Social Statistics
tech.description: Summarizes survey data in tables and regressions, and tests whether a gap between groups is larger than chance would leave.

tech.name: SOCY 140 · Qualitative Research Methods
tech.description: Interviews and observes people up close, under the ethics that requires. Coding the field notes takes longer than the fieldwork did.

tech.name: SOCY 210 · Criminology
tech.description: Tests theories of strain, control, and labeling against crime statistics and what the courts do with them.

tech.name: SOCY 220 · Sociology of the Family
tech.description: Marriage, parenting, and kinship vary by class and culture. None of them looks as it did a century ago.

tech.name: SOCY 230 · Race & Ethnicity
tech.description: Traces how racial and ethnic categories are drawn and contested, and follows their effects into housing, schooling, and the courts.

tech.name: SOCY 240 · Sex & Gender
tech.description: Treats gender as something societies build and then enforce at work and at home. Sexuality complicates the picture.

tech.name: SOCY 310 · Senior Thesis in Sociology
tech.description: Poses a question about social life and answers it with data the student gathers or finds. The paper is written to a journal's standards and reviewed the way a journal would.

tech.name: ANTH 101 · Introduction to Anthropology
tech.description: Meets the four fields in turn: cultural, biological, linguistic, and archaeological. Each arrives with the one case it explains best.

tech.name: ANTH 110 · Cultural Anthropology
tech.description: Kinship, ritual, and exchange look different in every society. Ethnography is how anyone knows, and what fieldwork cannot see is studied too.

tech.name: ANTH 120 · Biological Anthropology
tech.description: Reconstructs human evolution from fossil casts and living primates. Genetics fills in what bones cannot, including how modern humans came to vary.

tech.name: ANTH 130 · Archaeological Methods
tech.description: Surveys a site, digs it by layer, and dates what comes up. The harder step is turning broken things into claims about the past.

tech.name: ANTH 140 · Linguistic Anthropology
tech.description: Listens to dialect and politeness for what they say about a culture, and counts what is lost when a language dies.

tech.name: ANTH 210 · Ethnographic Field Methods
tech.description: Carries out a small ethnographic project, from gaining access to writing up, with the ethics at every step.

tech.name: ANTH 220 · Medical Anthropology
tech.description: Compares how cultures understand illness and healing, and what that means when medicine is delivered across the difference.

tech.name: ANTH 230 · Anthropology of Religion
tech.description: Studies myth, ritual, and magic. The standing argument is whether to explain them as Durkheim did or interpret them as Geertz did.

tech.name: ANTH 240 · History of Anthropological Theory
tech.description: Reads Boas, Malinowski, Evans-Pritchard, and Lévi-Strauss in turn. Each changed what an ethnographer goes into the field to find.

tech.name: ANTH 310 · Senior Seminar in Anthropology
tech.description: Turns a season of fieldwork, a museum collection, or a skeletal sample into an argued paper, presented to the department.

tech.name: POLS 101 · Introduction to Political Science
tech.description: Asks who gets what, when, and how. States, parties, and elections are the usual answers.

tech.name: POLS 110 · Comparative Politics
tech.description: Lines countries up by regime and party system to explain why some democracies last and some dictatorships do too.

tech.name: POLS 120 · International Relations
tech.description: Explains one war three ways, as a realist, a liberal, and a constructivist would, then does the same for trade and alliances.

tech.name: POLS 130 · American Government
tech.description: Takes the Constitution as a design for separated powers and federalism, and watches parties and interest groups work the machinery.

tech.name: POLS 140 · Research Methods in Political Science
tech.description: Designs a study of one political question and learns to read the regression tables the field publishes.

tech.name: POLS 210 · Constitutional Law
tech.description: Reads the landmark cases on judicial review, federal power, and civil liberties. Doctrine, it turns out, changes when the Court does.

tech.name: POLS 220 · Public Policy Analysis
tech.description: Defines a policy problem, weighs alternatives with cost-benefit analysis and evidence, and explains why the best option often loses.

tech.name: POLS 230 · Theories of Justice
tech.description: Argues with Rawls, Nozick, and their critics over what a just distribution and a legitimate state would be.

tech.name: POLS 240 · Security Studies
tech.description: Asks what deters a war or a terrorist or a cyberattack, and whether the intelligence and defense institutions built for one can meet the others.

tech.name: POLS 310 · Senior Seminar in Political Science
tech.description: Tests one argument about politics against cases or data the student assembles, in a paper defended before the seminar.

tech.name: Humanities Research Institute
tech.description: Archives, reading rooms and a documents collection. The History program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: HIST 101 · World History
tech.description: Compares how farming and empire arose in Afro-Eurasia and in the Americas, up to the contact that bound them into one world.

tech.name: HIST 110 · Research & Historiography
tech.description: Builds an argument from primary sources, and reads how Marxist, Annales, and cultural historians have told the same past differently.

tech.name: HIST 120 · US History
tech.description: Follows the Revolution, the Civil War and Reconstruction, the New Deal, and civil rights as one long argument over who counts as a citizen.

tech.name: HIST 130 · European History
tech.description: Watches the Reformation and the French Revolution build Europe's nation-states, whose rivalries lead the syllabus to 1914 and then to 1939.

tech.name: HIST 140 · Ancient Civilizations
tech.description: Studies Mesopotamia, Egypt, Greece, and Rome through the texts and the ruins each left behind.

tech.name: HIST 210 · World War I & II
tech.description: Works through the two world wars from their causes to their peace settlements, at the front and at home.

tech.name: HIST 220 · Modern East Asia
tech.description: Sees the Opium Wars, the Meiji reforms, colonial rule, and revolution as China, Japan, and Korea recorded them, in their own sources in translation.

tech.name: HIST 230 · Historical Anthropology
tech.description: Reads village feuds, witch trials, and carnival as an anthropologist would, working from court and parish records instead of fieldwork.

tech.name: HIST 240 · History of Science & Technology
tech.description: Traces how scientific ideas and machines have won acceptance since the Scientific Revolution, seldom as quickly as the textbooks suggest.

tech.name: HIST 310 · Senior Thesis in History
tech.description: Writes a thesis from primary sources in an archive and defends it before two faculty readers. Every footnote has to be one a referee could check.

tech.name: PHIL 101 · Introduction to Logic & Reasoning
tech.description: Puts arguments into standard form, tests their validity, and names the fallacies that make bad ones persuasive.

tech.name: PHIL 110 · Ethics
tech.description: Tries utilitarian, deontological, and virtue theories of right action on hard moral cases, where each one eventually says something its defenders regret.

tech.name: PHIL 120 · Metaphysics
tech.description: Asks whether numbers and possible worlds exist the way tables do, and what makes something the same thing over time or an action free.

tech.name: PHIL 130 · Epistemology
tech.description: Works out what it takes to know something and not merely believe it, against a skeptic who doubts that anyone does.

tech.name: PHIL 140 · Ancient Greek Philosophy
tech.description: Begins where philosophy did, with the Presocratics, Plato, and Aristotle on nature, knowledge, the soul, and the good life.

tech.name: PHIL 210 · Existentialism
tech.description: No guarantee of meaning is on offer. Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Heidegger, Sartre, and de Beauvoir are read on freedom, anxiety, and authenticity in its absence.

tech.name: PHIL 220 · Philosophy of Mind
tech.description: Asks how a brain gives rise to experience and how thoughts come to be about anything, then asks both of a machine.

tech.name: PHIL 230 · Early Modern Philosophy
tech.description: Reads Descartes, Spinoza, Locke, Hume, and Kant on what the mind can know of the world. Reason and experience each claimed to have settled it.

tech.name: PHIL 240 · Symbolic Logic
tech.description: Develops propositional and first-order logic with proofs and models, up to the completeness theorem and Gödel's limits on what such systems can prove.

tech.name: PHIL 310 · Senior Seminar in Philosophy
tech.description: Writes and revises one long paper defending a single thesis against the strongest objections the seminar can raise, and the seminar enjoys raising them.

tech.name: MATH 101 · Calculus
tech.description: Applies limits, derivatives, and integrals to related rates, optimization, and area. The fundamental theorem shows the two halves were one subject all along.

tech.name: MATH 110 · Linear Algebra
tech.description: Handles vector spaces, matrices, eigenvalues, and linear maps, geometry first, then the applications other departments send their students for.

tech.name: MATH 120 · Probability & Statistics
tech.description: Develops random variables and their distributions as far as the central limit theorem, and puts them to work in estimation and hypothesis testing.

tech.name: MATH 130 · Discrete Mathematics
tech.description: Proves things about logic, sets, graphs, and counting, usually by induction. It is the mathematics underneath computing.

tech.name: MATH 140 · Differential Equations
tech.description: Solves ordinary differential equations on paper where that is possible and numerically where it is not, modeling oscillators and populations.

tech.name: MATH 210 · Real Analysis
tech.description: Builds the real numbers, limits, continuity, and the integral from the axioms up. Every theorem calculus took on trust now has to be proved.

tech.name: MATH 220 · Abstract Algebra
tech.description: Studies the algebra of symmetry in groups and then rings and fields, far enough to show why no formula in radicals solves every quintic.

tech.name: MATH 230 · Topology
tech.description: Defines continuity by open sets alone, with no distances anywhere. By the end the fundamental group can tell a sphere from a torus.

tech.name: MATH 240 · Numerical Methods
tech.description: Analyzes algorithms for root finding, integration, linear systems, and differential equations, with the error and stability of each.

tech.name: MATH 310 · Senior Seminar in Mathematics
tech.description: Masters a recent paper or a classic proof and presents it to the seminar. The written exposition has to be one another student could follow.

tech.name: Biology Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Biology program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: BIOL 101 · Principles of Biology
tech.description: Starts with cells and genes and ends with evolution and ecosystems, with a weekly lab of microscopes, pipettes, and fruit flies.

tech.name: BIOL 110 · Cell Biology
tech.description: Tours the cell from its membrane inward, pairing each organelle and signal with the experiment that first revealed it.

tech.name: BIOL 120 · Genetics
tech.description: Follows inheritance from Mendel's peas to the sequenced genome, and learns the molecular tools that made the second possible.

tech.name: BIOL 130 · Ecology
tech.description: Studies populations, communities, and ecosystems, with field work on how organisms interact with each other and their environment.

tech.name: BIOL 140 · Evolution
tech.description: Tests natural selection, genetic drift, and speciation against the fossil record and against the family trees read from DNA.

tech.name: BIOL 210 · Microbiology
tech.description: Grows, stains, and identifies bacteria in the lab. Lectures cover the microbes the lab leaves out, how pathogens cause disease, and how antibiotics fail.

tech.name: BIOL 220 · Marine Biology
tech.description: Studies life in the sea at every size between plankton and whales, and samples the coast at low tide whatever hour that falls.

tech.name: BIOL 230 · Plant Physiology
tech.description: Explains how a plant makes its sugar and lifts its water. Hormones time its growth and its answers to stress and season.

tech.name: BIOL 240 · Immunology
tech.description: Traces innate and adaptive immunity through antigen recognition, antibodies, and T cells. Vaccines, allergy, and autoimmune disease are the same system at work.

tech.name: BIOL 310 · Senior Research in Biology
tech.description: Runs an independent experiment in a faculty lab for a year. The poster and the thesis report the version that finally worked.

tech.name: Chemistry Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Chemistry program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: CHEM 101 · General Chemistry
tech.description: Balances equations, counts moles, and works through atomic structure, bonding, gases, and equilibrium, in a lab where yields rarely match the arithmetic.

tech.name: CHEM 110 · Inorganic Chemistry
tech.description: Learns what each block of the periodic table tends to do, with bonding theory and coordination complexes to explain it.

tech.name: CHEM 120 · Organic Chemistry
tech.description: Pushes electrons around carbon compounds until mechanisms can be predicted and not memorized, with synthesis and spectroscopy in the lab.

tech.name: CHEM 130 · Analytical Chemistry
tech.description: Measures by titration, chromatography, and spectroscopy. No result counts until it comes with the statistics that say how far to trust it.

tech.name: CHEM 140 · Physical Chemistry
tech.description: Develops thermodynamics, kinetics, and quantum mechanics as they apply to molecules, using more calculus than any earlier chemistry course.

tech.name: CHEM 210 · Biochemistry
tech.description: Treats the cell as a chemist would. Proteins, enzymes, and nucleic acids are the parts, and metabolism is what they do under regulation.

tech.name: CHEM 220 · Spectroscopy & Structure Determination
tech.description: Solves molecular structures from NMR, infrared, and mass spectra, or from X-ray diffraction on the days a crystal agrees to grow.

tech.name: CHEM 230 · Medicinal Chemistry
tech.description: Follows a drug from target and lead compound through structure-activity relationships to metabolism and dose.

tech.name: CHEM 240 · Computational Chemistry
tech.description: Models molecules with quantum chemistry and molecular dynamics, and learns what each method can and cannot predict.

tech.name: CHEM 310 · Senior Research in Chemistry
tech.description: Joins a faculty research group to make or measure something new. The notebook is kept to the group's standard, and the thesis is written out of it.

tech.name: Physics Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Physics program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: PHYS 101 · Classical Mechanics
tech.description: Derives motion, force, energy, and momentum from Newton's laws, with lab work throughout.

tech.name: PHYS 110 · Electricity & Magnetism
tech.description: Develops electric and magnetic fields through potentials and circuits to induction. Maxwell's equations arrive at the end, and light turns out to be a consequence.

tech.name: PHYS 120 · Waves & Optics
tech.description: Asks what waves do that particles cannot. Interference and diffraction show up first in sound and at last in laser light.

tech.name: PHYS 130 · Modern Physics
tech.description: Studies the experiments that forced physics to change its mind, and the relativity and quantum theory they left behind.

tech.name: PHYS 140 · Thermal & Statistical Physics
tech.description: Derives temperature, entropy, and the laws of thermodynamics from the statistics of many particles.

tech.name: PHYS 210 · Quantum Mechanics
tech.description: Develops the Schrödinger equation, operators, angular momentum, and spin. The hydrogen atom is solved in full, as one of the few systems that can be.

tech.name: PHYS 220 · Solid State Physics
tech.description: Explains why some solids conduct and others do not, starting from crystal structure and band theory. Every device in the room depends on the answer.

tech.name: PHYS 230 · Astrophysics & Cosmology
tech.description: Applies gravity, nuclear physics, and radiation to stars and galaxies. The age and makeup of the universe are read from its microwave background.

tech.name: PHYS 240 · Particle Physics
tech.description: Meets the Standard Model of quarks, leptons, and forces. Accelerators and detectors have spent decades trying to break it.

tech.name: PHYS 310 · Senior Thesis in Physics
tech.description: Carries one question further in a written thesis, after repeating classic experiments such as Millikan's oil drop and the Franck-Hertz tube.

tech.name: ENVS 101 · Introduction to Environmental Science
tech.description: Samples one local stream all semester and uses it to learn the carbon and water cycles, soils, biodiversity, and pollution.

tech.name: ENVS 110 · Earth Systems & Climate
tech.description: Traces where energy and carbon go once they enter the atmosphere, and how the ocean and the land set the pace of climate change.

tech.name: ENVS 120 · Ecosystem Ecology
tech.description: Measures energy flow and nutrient cycling through forests, grasslands, and wetlands, with field and lab methods.

tech.name: ENVS 130 · Environmental Chemistry
tech.description: Chases a pollutant after its release through the reactions that make acid rain and thin the ozone, to wherever it finally settles.

tech.name: ENVS 140 · Geographic Information Systems
tech.description: Stacks spatial data layers and classified satellite imagery into a map that answers one environmental question.

tech.name: ENVS 210 · Conservation Biology
tech.description: Applies population genetics and landscape ecology to protecting species and habitats, on budgets that never cover all of them.

tech.name: ENVS 220 · Hydrology & Water Resources
tech.description: Tracks water through a watershed as rain, runoff, groundwater, and flood. The allocation among competing users is settled elsewhere, usually in court.

tech.name: ENVS 230 · Atmospheric Science
tech.description: Climbs from radiation and cloud physics to numerical forecasting, with air pollution and climate dynamics along the way.

tech.name: ENVS 240 · Environmental Policy & Restoration
tech.description: Applies the Clean Water Act, the Endangered Species Act, and NEPA to a degraded site, as the first step in planning its cleanup and replanting.

tech.name: ENVS 310 · Environmental Science Capstone
tech.description: Studies a watershed, wetland, or brownfield for a community partner as a team. The data and recommendations go out in a public report with the partner's name on it.

tech.name: PSYC 101 · General Psychology
tech.description: Visits perception, memory, learning, development, personality, and mental illness, each through the experiments its findings rest on.

tech.name: PSYC 110 · Developmental Psychology
tech.description: Traces development from infancy to old age through the long-running studies that mapped each stage.

tech.name: PSYC 120 · Cognitive Psychology
tech.description: Infers how the mind pays attention and remembers from reaction times and errors, since nobody can watch it work.

tech.name: PSYC 130 · Abnormal Psychology
tech.description: Classifies mental disorders by the DSM and weighs the evidence on the causes and treatment of anxiety, depression, and psychosis.

tech.name: PSYC 140 · Research Methods in Psychology
tech.description: Designs experiments and surveys, analyzes their data, and confronts the replication problems of the field.

tech.name: PSYC 210 · Social Psychology
tech.description: Studies conformity, persuasion, prejudice, and group behavior through the classic experiments, including the ones that did not survive a rerun.

tech.name: PSYC 220 · Biopsychology
tech.description: Links behavior to the brain: neurotransmitters, hormones, sleep, and the effects of drugs and damage.

tech.name: PSYC 230 · Organizational Psychology
tech.description: Applies psychology to who gets hired and who stays motivated at work, and tests whether the personality quiz predicts either.

tech.name: PSYC 240 · Health Psychology
tech.description: Studies how stress and belief change the course of an illness, and which interventions change the stress and the belief.

tech.name: PSYC 310 · Senior Thesis in Psychology
tech.description: Preregisters and runs an original study with human participants. The report follows the format a psychology journal requires, whatever the result.

tech.name: PHLT 101 · Introduction to Public Health
tech.description: Compares two neighboring counties' death rates and asks how income, housing, and policy explain the gap.

tech.name: PHLT 110 · Epidemiology
tech.description: Measures disease in populations by incidence, prevalence, and risk. Cohort and case-control studies are designed to find its causes.

tech.name: PHLT 120 · Biostatistics
tech.description: Learns enough statistics on health data to read a clinical trial's results table and to doubt it in the right places.

tech.name: PHLT 130 · Health Policy & Management
tech.description: Follows the money through a health system, since who pays for care goes a long way to deciding who gets it.

tech.name: PHLT 140 · Environmental Health
tech.description: Traces illness back to air, water, chemicals, and food. Risk assessment and regulation are the tools that limit a population's exposure.

tech.name: PHLT 210 · Global Health
tech.description: Weighs which interventions do the most good where money is shortest, with vaccination campaigns and maternal care as the working cases.

tech.name: PHLT 220 · Health Promotion
tech.description: Designs a program to change a habit like smoking or skipped screenings, grounded in behavioral theory. The evaluation asks whether anyone changed, which the brochure alone rarely achieves.

tech.name: PHLT 230 · Community Health Assessment
tech.description: Gathers and analyzes local health data with community partners, and turns it into ranked priorities and an improvement plan.

tech.name: PHLT 240 · Maternal & Child Health
tech.description: Tracks maternal and infant mortality, preterm birth, and childhood immunization against the prenatal care, WIC, and Medicaid meant to improve them.

tech.name: PHLT 310 · Public Health Practicum
tech.description: Works a semester with a health department or clinic on a live problem, and delivers the analysis and the program plan its staff asked for.

tech.name: NURS 101 · Introduction to Professional Nursing
tech.description: Starts with a nurse's legal scope of practice and code of ethics, then hand hygiene, vital signs, and charting. Charting takes the longest to learn.

tech.name: NURS 110 · Anatomy & Physiology
tech.description: Learns every organ system twice, once at the dissection table for structure and once in lecture for function.

tech.name: NURS 120 · Pharmacology
tech.description: Sorts drugs by class, mechanism, and interaction. Before any dose is given, the patient, the drug, the route, and the time are checked again.

tech.name: NURS 130 · Health Assessment
tech.description: Takes a history and examines a patient head to toe, then writes the findings up, because a finding nobody charted did not happen.

tech.name: NURS 140 · Clinical Practicum I
tech.description: Goes onto a hospital ward under supervision and gives basic nursing care to patients for the first time.

tech.name: NURS 210 · Medical-Surgical Nursing
tech.description: Manages adults on hospital wards with heart failure, diabetes, pneumonia, or a fresh surgical wound, the core of nursing practice and of its licensing examination.

tech.name: NURS 220 · Pediatric Nursing
tech.description: Cares for infants, children, and adolescents, where doses go by weight and the conversation is usually with a parent.

tech.name: NURS 230 · Maternal & Newborn Nursing
tech.description: Follows a pregnancy through prenatal visits, labor and delivery, and the first days at home, caring for mother and newborn as two patients at once.

tech.name: NURS 240 · Psychiatric & Mental Health Nursing
tech.description: Forms a working relationship with patients in psychosis or withdrawal, and learns the risk assessment and de-escalation an inpatient unit runs on.

tech.name: NURS 310 · Capstone Clinical Practicum
tech.description: Runs a full patient load on a specialty unit under one preceptor for a term. The licensing examination comes next, and nobody needs reminding.

tech.name: NUTR 101 · Fundamentals of Nutrition
tech.description: Reads a food label line by line: the calories and protein first, then the vitamins whose shortfall still causes disease.

tech.name: NUTR 110 · Macronutrients & Metabolism
tech.description: Tracks carbohydrates, fats, and proteins from digestion through the metabolic pathways that store and burn them.

tech.name: NUTR 120 · Lifecycle Nutrition
tech.description: Matches nutrient needs to each life stage and its common shortfall: folate in pregnancy, iron in toddlers, protein in old age.

tech.name: NUTR 130 · Applied Dietetics
tech.description: Plans menus inside the limits of a low-sodium or texture-modified diet that a person would still want to eat, and documents each case in the nutrition care process.

tech.name: NUTR 140 · Food Science
tech.description: Explains what spoils food and what preserves it through its chemistry and microbiology. Cooking gets the same treatment.

tech.name: NUTR 210 · Sports Nutrition
tech.description: Fuels training and competition by planning energy, hydration, and timing. The supplements athletes take get evaluated on evidence, which thins the shelf considerably.

tech.name: NUTR 220 · Public Health Nutrition
tech.description: Addresses malnutrition and obesity at the population level, through food policy, school programs, and surveillance.

tech.name: NUTR 230 · Advanced Medical Nutrition Therapy
tech.description: Manages nutrition in diabetes, kidney disease, cancer, and critical illness, including tube and intravenous feeding.

tech.name: NUTR 240 · Nutrition Assessment & Counseling
tech.description: Assesses clients by anthropometric, biochemical, clinical, and dietary data. Counseling is by motivational interviewing, in supervised sessions.

tech.name: NUTR 310 · Supervised Practice in Dietetics
tech.description: Plans and delivers nutrition care for patients and for a community program under registered dietitians, and presents one case in full.

tech.name: PHRM 101 · Introduction to Pharmaceutical Sciences
tech.description: Follows one drug from its discovery through formulation to the pharmacist who hands it across the counter.

tech.name: PHRM 110 · Human Physiology for Pharmacy
tech.description: Revisits organ-system physiology with a pharmacist's emphasis, on the receptors and pathways that drugs act on.

tech.name: PHRM 120 · Pharmaceutical Chemistry
tech.description: Relates drug structure to activity, stability, and formulation, with the organic and analytical chemistry behind each.

tech.name: PHRM 130 · Pharmacology I
tech.description: Maps drug action on the nervous and cardiovascular systems: receptors, dose-response curves, and the agents used in each.

tech.name: PHRM 140 · Pharmaceutics & Drug Delivery
tech.description: Formulates tablets, injections, and patches around the kinetics of how a drug is absorbed, distributed, and cleared.

tech.name: PHRM 210 · Pharmacology II
tech.description: Extends drug action to infection, cancer, endocrine, and inflammatory disease, with toxicity and resistance.

tech.name: PHRM 220 · Pharmacotherapeutics
tech.description: Selects and monitors drug therapy for patient cases, where the textbook choice meets a second diagnosis and a long medication list.

tech.name: PHRM 230 · Clinical Pharmacy Practicum
tech.description: Shadows pharmacists in a hospital and a community pharmacy, reconciling medication lists and watching counseling done well.

tech.name: PHRM 240 · Pharmacoepidemiology & Drug Safety
tech.description: Studies drug effects after approval through adverse-event reports and claims data, and the boxed warnings and withdrawals they prompt.

tech.name: PHRM 310 · Senior Research in Pharmaceutical Sciences
tech.description: Runs a semester's project in a formulation or pharmacology lab, and presents the data as a drug company's project team would expect it.

tech.name: KINE 101 · Foundations of Kinesiology
tech.description: Treats human movement as one connected system of anatomy, physiology, and mechanics.

tech.name: KINE 110 · Functional Anatomy
tech.description: Finds each muscle, bone, and joint by touch on a lab partner. The harder exercise is naming the ones a squat or a throw is using.

tech.name: KINE 120 · Exercise Physiology
tech.description: Measures how the heart, lungs, and muscles respond to exercise, on a treadmill, in a mask, with classmates taking turns as the subject.

tech.name: KINE 130 · Biomechanics
tech.description: Applies forces and torques to the body with motion capture, analyzing everything from a golf swing to a fall.

tech.name: KINE 140 · Motor Learning & Control
tech.description: Asks how the nervous system acquires a skill, and why a practice schedule that feels worse often teaches better.

tech.name: KINE 210 · Strength & Conditioning
tech.description: Programs resistance and conditioning for athletes in periodized blocks, tests the results, and coaches lifting technique.

tech.name: KINE 220 · Athletic Injury & Rehabilitation
tech.description: Assesses and rehabilitates common sports injuries, from acute care and taping to return-to-play progressions.

tech.name: KINE 230 · Exercise Testing & Prescription
tech.description: Screens clients for risk, runs graded exercise tests, and prescribes frequency, intensity, time, and type by the American College of Sports Medicine's guidelines.

tech.name: KINE 240 · Adapted Physical Activity
tech.description: Adapts physical activity for people with disabilities and chronic conditions, with inclusion and safety as the starting points.

tech.name: KINE 310 · Kinesiology Internship
tech.description: Works a semester in a clinic or a training room under a certified professional, and documents each client's progress in notes someone else must be able to read.

tech.name: Neuroscience Labs
tech.description: Specialized lab space. The Neuroscience program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: NEUR 101 · Foundations of Neuroscience
tech.description: Follows a reflex, a memory, and a decision from the neurons that carry them to the behavior they produce.

tech.name: NEUR 110 · Neuroanatomy
tech.description: Maps the structures of the brain and spinal cord, their connections, and what damage to each does, with brain dissection in the lab.

tech.name: NEUR 120 · Cellular & Molecular Neuroscience
tech.description: Opens up a single neuron to see how it signals, starting at the ion channel and ending at the synapse.

tech.name: NEUR 130 · Cognitive Neuroscience
tech.description: Links perception, memory, language, and decision-making to brain systems, through imaging, lesion, and recording studies.

tech.name: NEUR 140 · Neurophysiology
tech.description: Records and analyzes electrical activity at three scales: the patch-clamped single cell, the circuit, and the scalp EEG.

tech.name: NEUR 210 · Neuropharmacology
tech.description: Compares how prescribed drugs and addictive ones act on the same neurotransmitter systems, to different ends.

tech.name: NEUR 220 · Developmental Neurobiology
tech.description: Traces how the nervous system is built, from neural induction and axon guidance to synapse formation and plasticity.

tech.name: NEUR 230 · Computational Neuroscience
tech.description: Models neurons and networks mathematically, from the Hodgkin-Huxley equations to learning rules and neural coding.

tech.name: NEUR 240 · Clinical Neuroscience & Disorders
tech.description: Traces stroke, epilepsy, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and psychiatric illness down to mechanism. Each mechanism is also where a treatment has to start.

tech.name: NEUR 310 · Senior Thesis in Neuroscience
tech.description: Carries an independent question through a year in a faculty lab and defends the result as a thesis, before an audience that knows the rig.

tech.name: Computing Research Center
tech.description: A compute cluster and research offices. The Computer Science program's advanced courses need it, and it lets the college produce research.

tech.name: COMP 101 · Introduction to Programming
tech.description: Writes small programs that read, loop, and decide. The other skill is finding the bugs before a grader does.

tech.name: COMP 110 · Data Structures
tech.description: Implements each standard structure by hand once. After that the skill is picking the one a problem needs and knowing what it will cost.

tech.name: COMP 120 · Algorithms
tech.description: Proves an algorithm correct and bounds its running time before trusting it, across sorting, graph search, dynamic programming, and greedy methods.

tech.name: COMP 130 · Operating Systems
tech.description: Learns what an operating system quietly does for every program, then writes concurrent code and finds out what it does not do.

tech.name: COMP 140 · Computer Architecture
tech.description: Goes below the compiler to the instruction set and the cache, where the hardware decides which software runs fast.

tech.name: COMP 210 · Compiler Design
tech.description: Writes a compiler stage by stage, from lexing and parsing through type checking and optimization to code that runs on an actual processor.

tech.name: COMP 220 · Game Development
tech.description: Builds a playable game as a team, with a rendering loop, physics, input, and the design iteration that makes it fun.

tech.name: COMP 230 · Parallel Computing
tech.description: Programs multicore, GPU, and distributed systems with threads and message passing. The last step is measuring the speedup actually obtained.

tech.name: COMP 240 · Web Development
tech.description: Ships a full-stack web application to outside users, with authentication, caching, load testing, and the attacks a public site has to withstand.

tech.name: COMP 310 · Senior Thesis in Computer Science
tech.description: Pursues one research question with a faculty adviser, and writes up as a thesis whatever the literature and the experiments turn out to support.

tech.name: DATA 101 · Fundamentals of Data Science
tech.description: Takes a messy public dataset from download to a first chart, cleaning and questioning it at every step.

tech.name: DATA 110 · Statistical Modeling
tech.description: Fits linear and generalized linear models and checks their assumptions before reading what the coefficients do and do not claim.

tech.name: DATA 120 · Machine Learning
tech.description: Trains and evaluates regression, trees, clustering, and neural networks. The bias-variance trade-off turns up in every one of them.

tech.name: DATA 130 · Data Visualization
tech.description: Draws charts and interactive graphics that make a dataset's structure legible, and learns what makes a visualization mislead.

tech.name: DATA 140 · Data Mining
tech.description: Finds patterns in large datasets with association rules, clustering, and anomaly detection. The second job is checking that they are not accidents of the sample.

tech.name: DATA 210 · Big Data Systems
tech.description: Splits storage and computation across a cluster, and decides when a batch job, a stream, or one large server is the cheaper way to an answer.

tech.name: DATA 220 · Time Series Analysis
tech.description: Separates trend from seasonality and autocorrelation with ARIMA and state-space methods, and forecasts with honest uncertainty.

tech.name: DATA 230 · Natural Language Processing
tech.description: Gets a program to read and write text, with n-gram counts first and transformer language models by the end.

tech.name: DATA 240 · Bayesian Statistics
tech.description: Starts from a prior belief, updates it with data by the rules of probability, and lets small groups such as counties borrow strength from one another.

tech.name: DATA 310 · Data Science Capstone
tech.description: Answers a partner organization's question with its own data, cleaned, modeled, and explained to managers who never asked for a p-value.

tech.name: CYBR 101 · Introduction to Cybersecurity
tech.description: Learns who attacks computer systems and why, and that plain habits like patching and backups stop most of them.

tech.name: CYBR 110 · Network Security
tech.description: Secures networks with firewalls, intrusion detection, VPNs, and protocol hardening, against attacks run in a lab.

tech.name: CYBR 120 · Cryptography
tech.description: Works through symmetric and public-key ciphers, hashes, signatures, and protocols. Sound mathematics still fails in careless code.

tech.name: CYBR 130 · Ethical Hacking
tech.description: Breaks into systems with written permission, working up from reconnaissance to privilege escalation, then writes the report that makes the findings fixable.

tech.name: CYBR 140 · Security Operations
tech.description: Staffs a security operations center: log analysis, monitoring, incident response, and the playbooks for when something gets through.

tech.name: CYBR 210 · Cloud Security
tech.description: Secures identity, storage, networking, and workloads on public cloud platforms, where a misconfiguration is the usual cause of a breach.

tech.name: CYBR 220 · Digital Forensics
tech.description: Pulls evidence off disks and out of memory and network traffic, handled so that it holds up in court.

tech.name: CYBR 230 · Security Risk Management
tech.description: Ranks which threats and vulnerabilities deserve a control first, and maps the controls to the compliance frameworks an organization is audited against.

tech.name: CYBR 240 · Software Security Testing
tech.description: Finds vulnerabilities in code by static analysis, fuzzing, and review. Keeping the next ones out is a matter of habit, which is harder.

tech.name: CYBR 310 · Cyber Defense Capstone
tech.description: Defends a simulated company network against a live attacking team for a term, and writes the incident reports and the remediation plan.

tech.name: SOFT 101 · Introduction to Software Development
tech.description: Writes small programs in a team under version control and code review, and ships one of them against a written requirement.

tech.name: SOFT 110 · Software Requirements
tech.description: Elicits, specifies, and validates what a system must do, with stakeholders who disagree and needs that change.

tech.name: SOFT 120 · Software Testing & QA
tech.description: Tests a system at every level and automates the tests. Coverage and defect rates say something about quality, though less than a dashboard implies.

tech.name: SOFT 130 · Database Systems
tech.description: Designs relational schemas and queries them in SQL, and learns which guarantees a database makes about a transaction and which it does not.

tech.name: SOFT 140 · Object-Oriented Design
tech.description: Applies design patterns, SOLID principles, and refactoring to build systems that survive being changed.

tech.name: SOFT 210 · Agile Methodologies
tech.description: Runs a project in sprints with a product backlog, stand-ups, and retrospectives. The last retrospective asks what agile fixes and what it hides.

tech.name: SOFT 220 · Mobile Application Development
tech.description: Builds native apps for phones, where the screen is small and the battery is finite and the network comes and goes.

tech.name: SOFT 230 · UI/UX
tech.description: Carries an interface from user research through prototypes to usability testing, with accessibility as a requirement rather than an afterthought.

tech.name: SOFT 240 · DevOps
tech.description: Automates build, test, and deployment pipelines with containers, infrastructure as code, and monitoring, so that releases become routine.

tech.name: SOFT 310 · Software Engineering Capstone
tech.description: Delivers a working product for an outside client as a team, through requirements, sprints, and testing. It is finished when the client is running it.

tech.name: ARTF 101 · Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
tech.description: Surveys search, logic, probabilistic reasoning, and learning from data, and the two funding winters that followed when the field overpromised.

tech.name: ARTF 110 · AI Programming
tech.description: Implements classical search and probabilistic reasoning in code, the toolkit still running under modern systems.

tech.name: ARTF 120 · Knowledge Representation
tech.description: Encodes facts and rules in logics and ontologies, reasons over them with inference engines, and finds where those give out.

tech.name: ARTF 130 · Neural Networks
tech.description: Builds and trains multilayer networks from backpropagation up. Without optimization and regularization they learn nothing useful, so those come next.

tech.name: ARTF 140 · Statistical Learning
