tech.description: Fits decision trees and then the random forests and boosted ensembles built from them. Each is judged only on data it has not seen.

tech.name: ARTF 210 · Deep Learning
tech.description: Trains convolutional, recurrent, and transformer networks at scale, where the hard part is feeding the GPUs and keeping a week-long run alive.

tech.name: ARTF 220 · Robotics & Perception
tech.description: Gives a robot senses and plans, through localization, mapping, motion planning, and control, on hardware that does not always do as it is told.

tech.name: ARTF 230 · Computer Vision
tech.description: Finds and names objects in images and video, first with hand-built features and then with the deep networks that replaced them.

tech.name: ARTF 240 · AI Ethics & Society
tech.description: Asks who answers when deployed AI discriminates, surveils, or displaces workers, and whether the governance proposed so far would change it.

tech.name: ARTF 310 · Artificial Intelligence Capstone
tech.description: Builds and evaluates an AI system for a task someone needs done, with the baseline it must beat and an audit of where it fails and whom that harms.

tech.name: INFO 101 · Introduction to Information Systems
tech.description: Walks one order through the web store, the database, the warehouse software, and the general ledger, asking at each stop who owns the system.

tech.name: INFO 110 · Systems Analysis & Design
tech.description: Models an organization's processes and data, and specifies the information system that would serve them, with the stakeholders in the room.

tech.name: INFO 120 · Database Management
tech.description: Keeps a production database running through schema changes, slow queries, and restores from backup. A non-relational store has to earn its place.

tech.name: INFO 130 · Enterprise Resource Planning
tech.description: Configures an enterprise system across finance, supply chain, and HR. The reading list is on why so many implementations overrun.

tech.name: INFO 140 · IT Infrastructure
tech.description: Provisions and secures the servers and cloud services an organization runs on, and reads the monthly bill for them.

tech.name: INFO 210 · Business Process Modeling
tech.description: Maps and redesigns workflows with process notation and simulation, and counts the handoffs and waiting time a redesign removes.

tech.name: INFO 220 · E-commerce Strategy
tech.description: Analyzes online business models down to payments and logistics, to find what makes a digital marketplace defensible.

tech.name: INFO 230 · Information Security Management
tech.description: Drafts an organization's security program: policy, risk assessment, staff awareness, and governance under regulation.

tech.name: INFO 240 · Data Warehousing
tech.description: Designs dimensional models and ETL pipelines that feed analytics and reporting, so that two dashboards asked the same question give the same number.

tech.name: INFO 310 · Information Systems Capstone
tech.description: Scopes, budgets, and manages an information-systems project for a partner organization, through rollout and the training of the people who will use it.

tech.name: MED 501 · Foundations of Human Medicine
tech.description: Opens medical training with the body as one system and with the patient interview, which will be practiced for the rest of a career. Founds the medical school.

tech.name: MED 510 · Gross Anatomy & Histology
tech.description: Dissects alongside the microscope, so that each structure is learned both where it lies and by what its tissue is made of.

tech.name: MED 520 · Pathophysiology & Pharmacotherapy
tech.description: Pairs each disease's mechanism with the drugs that interrupt it, so that a dose and its side effects are learned with the illness they treat.

tech.name: MED 530 · Clinical Neurology
tech.description: Localizes the lesion from the bedside examination before looking at the scan, a point of pride in neurology, across stroke, seizure, and disorders of movement.

tech.name: MED 540 · Evidence-Based Practice & Population Medicine
tech.description: Takes clinical trials apart at journal club, limitations first. The question each time is whether the evidence should change practice for one patient or for a population.

tech.name: MED 550 · Internal Medicine
tech.description: Reasons through an adult patient's complaint to a diagnosis across the heart, lungs, kidneys, and gut. The plan is presented on morning rounds, where it is improved aloud.

tech.name: MED 560 · Immunology & Infectious Disease
tech.description: Follows the contest between an immune system that recognizes and remembers and the pathogens that evade it, with vaccines and antimicrobials tipping the balance.

tech.name: MED 570 · Medical Genetics & Genomics
tech.description: Reads a family pedigree and an exome sequence as clinical evidence. Each result then has to be explained to the family it belongs to.

tech.name: MED 580 · Psychiatry & Behavioral Medicine
tech.description: Diagnoses and treats mental illness alongside the behaviors, from sleep to substance use, that shape every other illness a patient has.

tech.name: MED 590 · Surgical Principles & Perioperative Care
tech.description: Learns the operating room in order: consent, sterile technique, anesthesia, and the healing and complications of the days after. The student's first job is to hold the retractor.

tech.name: MED 600 · Transition to Clerkships
tech.description: Practices note-writing, case presentations, and handoffs before the wards, so a student can be useful before being knowledgeable.

tech.name: MED 610 · Advanced Clinical Practicum
tech.description: Rotates through internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, and family medicine. The year ends as a sub-intern, with patients of the student's own and the pager that comes with them.

tech.name: LAW 501 · Foundations of American Law
tech.description: Learns where American law comes from and how courts reason from precedent, and briefs a case for every class in the expectation of being called on. Founds the law school.

tech.name: LAW 510 · Contracts & Torts
tech.description: Asks when a promise binds and what breaking it costs, then when an act becomes a wrong. The reasonable person is consulted throughout.

tech.name: LAW 520 · Civil Procedure & Evidence
tech.description: Follows a lawsuit from the complaint through discovery and trial, and the rules that decide which facts a jury is ever allowed to hear.

tech.name: LAW 530 · American Constitutional Law
tech.description: Turns the Commerce Clause, due process, and equal protection into tests a brief can apply. Moot court supplies the bench, and the bench interrupts.

tech.name: LAW 540 · Professional Responsibility
tech.description: Works through the rules of professional conduct on conflicts, confidentiality, and candor to the court. The hard cases set a lawyer's duty to a client against the duty to the law.

tech.name: LAW 550 · Property & Real Estate Law
tech.description: Sorts out who owns land and on what terms. A title search and a mortgage lead to the closing, where real estate finally changes hands and everyone signs everything.

tech.name: LAW 560 · Criminal Law & Procedure
tech.description: Defines what makes conduct a crime, and holds the state to the constitutional limits on search, interrogation, and trial in proving it.

tech.name: LAW 570 · Legal Clinic & Advocacy
tech.description: Represents the clinic's clients under supervision: drafting, negotiating, and appearing in court. The cases are the college's, and so are the filing deadlines.

tech.name: MBA 501 · Managerial Foundations
tech.description: Learns enough accounting, economics, and organizational behavior that a class of engineers, bankers, and poets can argue a case in one vocabulary. Founds the MBA program.

tech.name: MBA 510 · Corporate Finance & Valuation
tech.description: Decides how a firm should raise money, spend it, and return it, one case at a time. The valuation has to be ready before class, in the event of a cold call.

tech.name: MBA 520 · Marketing Strategy
tech.description: Chooses which customers to serve and how to win them against rivals, from segmentation and positioning to pricing and brand.

tech.name: MBA 530 · Operations & Business Analytics
tech.description: Models supply chains and queues with a firm's own data, to decide where the business should cut waste and where it should add slack.

tech.name: MBA 540 · Capstone Consulting Practicum
tech.description: Advises an outside organization on a live problem as a team, and presents the recommendations to its leadership in fewer slides than the team wanted.

tech.name: PHDE 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Engineering
tech.description: Frames a research question, designs the experiments and simulations to answer it, and defends the result to peers who know where to push. Founds the engineering doctorate.

tech.name: PHDE 710 · Advanced Continuum & Structural Theory
tech.description: Derives the mechanics of solids and fluids from first principles, and applies them to structures and materials at the limits of design.

tech.name: PHDE 720 · Doctoral Seminar in Applied Electromagnetics
tech.description: Treats wave propagation, antennas, and electromagnetic compatibility at research depth, with papers from the field presented each week.

tech.name: PHDE 730 · Dissertation Research in Engineering
tech.description: Registers the candidate each term until the experiments are done, the chapters are written, and the committee signs off.

tech.name: PHDS 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in the Sciences
tech.description: Learns experimental design, statistics, and research ethics before the first laboratory project, which is the cheapest time to learn them. Founds the natural-sciences doctorate.

tech.name: PHDS 710 · Advanced Quantum & Statistical Theory
tech.description: Raises quantum mechanics and statistical physics to the level where current research papers in either field can be read and extended.

tech.name: PHDS 720 · Advanced Synthesis & Structure Determination
tech.description: Plans multistep syntheses and proves what was made, with spectroscopy and crystallography read directly from the instruments.

tech.name: PHDS 730 · Dissertation Research in the Natural Sciences
tech.description: Ends in a public defense and the graduate school's acceptance of the final copy, after however many years the research takes.

tech.name: PHDH 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Health Science
tech.description: Designs a study of patients or a population, with the biostatistics to power it and the ethics protocol a review board will read line by line. Founds the health-science doctorate.

tech.name: PHDH 710 · Systems & Cognitive Neuroscience Seminar
tech.description: Presents and critiques current papers on the circuits behind cognition, weighing what imaging, optogenetics, and population recording can each show about cause.

tech.name: PHDH 720 · Translational Clinical Research
tech.description: Carries a finding from the laboratory into a clinical trial, with the regulatory, statistical, and ethical steps between the two.

tech.name: PHDH 730 · Dissertation Research in Health Science
tech.description: Takes a question of the student's own through a proposal, data collection, and three publishable papers to the final defense.

tech.name: PHDC 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Computing
tech.description: Reads the literature, runs reproducible experiments, and writes papers that computing conferences will accept. Founds the computing doctorate.

tech.name: PHDC 710 · Advanced Seminar in Learning Theory
tech.description: Studies what can be learned from data and how fast, with the generalization bounds and optimization results behind modern machine learning.

tech.name: PHDC 720 · Foundations of Computation
tech.description: Works through computability and complexity classes to the limits they set on what any algorithm, however clever, can ever achieve.

tech.name: PHDC 730 · Dissertation Research in Computing
tech.description: Turns a series of peer-reviewed conference papers into a dissertation, with the experiments rerun until a committee is satisfied.

tech.name: PHDL 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in the Humanities
tech.description: Enters the archive, reads closely, and learns the conventions of scholarly argument, the footnote above all. Founds the humanities doctorate.

tech.name: PHDL 710 · Advanced Seminar in Literary Theory
tech.description: Reads Derrida, Foucault, and Spivak whole rather than in excerpt. The affective and ecological turns that have since argued with them come after.

tech.name: PHDL 720 · Doctoral Seminar in Social Theory
tech.description: Sets Durkheim, Weber, Bourdieu, and Habermas against one another on how societies hold together, change, and divide.

tech.name: PHDL 730 · Dissertation Research in the Humanities
tech.description: Writes the dissertation itself, a book-length work of original scholarship, defended before a committee that has read every draft.

tech.name: PhD 701 · Doctoral Research Methods in Economics
tech.description: Drills the econometrics, identification strategies, and data work that doctoral research in economics is judged on, usually in the first seminar question. Founds the economics doctorate.

tech.name: PhD 710 · Advanced Microeconomic Theory
tech.description: Builds consumer, producer, and general-equilibrium theory with the mathematics used in current research, from game theory to mechanism design.

tech.name: PhD 720 · Doctoral Seminar in Financial Economics
tech.description: Presents current research on asset pricing, corporate finance, and financial crises to the seminar, one student and one paper each week.

tech.name: PhD 730 · Dissertation Research in Economics
tech.description: Assembles three original papers into a dissertation, and sends the strongest out as the job-market paper a candidate presents at every interview.

tech.name: MFA 701 · Graduate Studio Practice
tech.description: Works in a studio of the artist's own and brings the results to a weekly critique, where peers and faculty argue over them at length. Founds the MFA program.

tech.name: MFA 710 · Advanced Fiction & Poetry Workshop
tech.description: Critiques a new manuscript from each writer every few weeks, alongside craft reading chosen for what that writer's work is attempting.

tech.name: MFA 720 · Graduate Composition Seminar
tech.description: Brings new scores before performers and peers each week, and learns from the performers which bars cannot be played as written.

tech.name: MFA 730 · Thesis Exhibition & Production
tech.description: Mounts a public exhibition, performance, or publication to close the degree. The faculty review it, and so does everyone at the opening.

tech.name: Meadow House
tech.description: The college's first residence hall.

tech.name: Lakeside House
tech.description: A house of entryways rather than corridors, with an RA on the first floor of each. Freshmen ask for these by name. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Riverside House
tech.description: A residence hall: four stories of ranked windows and balconies under one long roof. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Hillcrest House
tech.description: Suites behind a real front door: quieter than the halls, with a kitchenette to each floor and a lounge nobody books. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Cascade House
tech.description: An apartment building, flat-roofed and balconied: kitchens and a lock on every door, the kind of housing upperclassmen ask for. Adds 500 beds.

tech.name: Summit House
tech.description: A residential college: a thousand beds around one formal front door, built in the stone the college keeps for its best. The old answer to everything, at the old price. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Vanguard House
tech.description: A six-story apartment building with a balcony to every other apartment. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Sterling House
tech.description: A high-rise residence hall: twice the beds on more ground, six stories of ranked windows and balconies. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Crestline House
tech.description: Six stories of suites behind a formal door: the residence seniors ask for. Adds 1,000 beds.

tech.name: Overlook Village
tech.description: A residential village: a dozen small houses around a shared green, on one large plot. Adds 1,500 beds.

tech.name: Ridgeline Village
tech.description: A residential village in brick: a dozen houses and a common house around a shared green, on one large plot. Adds 1,500 beds.

tech.name: Meridian Tower
tech.description: A residential tower with shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: Beacon Tower
tech.description: A residential tower lit at the top, with shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: Horizon Tower
tech.description: A residential tower with a roof terrace, and shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: Aurora Tower
tech.description: The tallest residential tower on campus, under a glass crown, with shops and a food hall at street level. Adds 5,000 beds, and feeds 1,500 students from its shops.

tech.name: The Original Commons
tech.description: The first dining hall, where the college learned what students will and won't eat on a Tuesday.

tech.name: Coffee Kiosk
tech.description: A coffee counter under a striped awning, with two café tables and a queue at ten to nine.

tech.name: Union Square Eatery
tech.description: Another dining hall, with longer opening hours and the same argument about the waffle iron.

tech.name: Hilltop Cafeteria
tech.description: Another dining hall, with longer opening hours and the same argument about the waffle iron.

tech.name: Food Truck Plaza
tech.description: Four food trucks parked round a paved square of picnic tables under string lights. The menu changes with the trucks.

tech.name: The Grand Table
tech.description: A small trattoria with a wood-fired oven, checked tablecloths and a terrace under a vine. Students book it for birthdays.

tech.name: Old Well Hall
tech.description: Another dining hall, with longer opening hours and the same argument about the waffle iron.

tech.name: Waterside Market Hall
tech.description: Another dining hall, with longer opening hours and the same argument about the waffle iron.

tech.name: Harborview Market
tech.description: Another dining hall, with longer opening hours and the same argument about the waffle iron.

tech.name: Central Dining Pavilion
tech.description: Another dining hall, with longer opening hours and the same argument about the waffle iron.

tech.name: Campus Grocery Store
tech.description: A full grocery store, for students who have discovered they can cook one thing.

tech.name: Library
tech.description: Stacks, carrels and a quiet floor that is quiet in principle.

tech.name: Student Center
tech.description: Lounges, a coffee counter and the bulletin board every club fights over.

tech.name: Student Union Expansion
tech.description: A second wing for the Student Center, with a ballroom nobody can book.

tech.name: Recreation Center
tech.description: Courts, a climbing wall and intramural leagues that take themselves very seriously.

tech.name: Gym & Fitness Center
tech.description: A weight room and a cardio floor, busiest the first week of every term.

tech.name: Swimming Pool
tech.description: An outdoor Olympic-length pool and its deck, open from the first warm day to the first cold one.

tech.name: Tennis Courts
tech.description: Hard courts behind a tall fence, booked solid by a small number of very keen people.

tech.name: Sports & Recreation Complex
tech.description: The fitness complex that finishes the set: more courts, more machines, a smoothie bar.

tech.name: Art Gallery
tech.description: A white-walled gallery with rotating shows, where Studio Art's seniors hang their exhibition.

tech.name: Campus Radio
tech.description: A small studio under a tall mast with a red light on top. Students run the shows through the night, and the advanced Media Studies courses are taught here.

tech.name: The Pub
tech.description: A wood-paneled pub with a dartboard, a quiz night on Tuesdays and a beer garden out the back.

tech.name: Bowling Alley
tech.description: Sixteen lanes, rented shoes and a league whose standings are followed more closely than the football team's.

tech.name: Movie Theater
tech.description: Three screens under a lit marquee, with new films on the weekend and old ones for a dollar on Wednesdays.

tech.name: Basketball Courts
tech.description: Outdoor courts with chain nets, where pickup games run until the floodlights go off.

tech.name: Multi-Sport Field
tech.description: A competition field for soccer, lacrosse, field hockey and track, with lines repainted every week.

tech.name: Arena
tech.description: An indoor arena shared by basketball, volleyball and ice hockey, on a schedule none of them likes.

tech.name: Baseball & Softball Diamond
tech.description: A regulation diamond shared by baseball and softball, and a bleacher with opinions.

tech.name: Natatorium
tech.description: An indoor competition pool for swim & dive and water polo, kept at a temperature only swimmers enjoy.

tech.name: Football Stadium
tech.description: A football stadium, the largest building on campus and the one alumni can find without a map.

tech.name: Field House
tech.description: Weight rooms, an indoor training floor and treatment rooms for every varsity program.

tech.name: Health & Counseling Center
tech.description: Appointments, a nurse on call and a waiting room full of pamphlets.

tech.name: University Clinic
tech.description: Full outpatient care, and where Nursing and Pharmacy students do their clinical work.

tech.name: Medical Center
tech.description: A teaching hospital with the college's name over the door, and home of the MD.

tech.name: Campus Quad
tech.description: A lawn at the middle of campus, crossed on the diagonal by everyone who is late.

tech.name: Grand Quad & Gardens
tech.description: Formal gardens around the quad, with paths laid where the students had already walked.

tech.name: The Founder's Statue
tech.description: The founder in bronze on a stone plinth, a little larger than life, and a meeting place from the day it goes up.

tech.name: The Gazebo
tech.description: An open eight-sided pavilion with a railing and a pointed roof: where the band plays on summer evenings, and where half the campus has been proposed to.

tech.name: The Fountain
tech.description: A basin and a jet on a paved circle: somewhere to sit, and the first photograph on every tour.

tech.name: The Japanese Garden
tech.description: A koi pond under a red bridge, a torii over the path, a three-tiered pagoda, a stone lantern and cherry trees in blossom: the quietest acre on campus.

tech.name: The Chapel
tech.description: A small stone chapel, used for concerts and quiet as often as for services.

tech.name: The Bell Tower
tech.description: A slim tower with a peal of bells that marks the hours across the campus.

tech.name: The Parterre
tech.description: Low box hedges clipped into knots around gravel walks and a sundial, laid out to be looked down on from the windows.

tech.name: The Amphitheater
tech.description: Grass terraces stepped down to a small stone stage, for plays in June and for lectures outdoors when the heating fails.

tech.name: The Sculpture Garden
tech.description: Bronze and steel on plinths across a mown lawn, each piece the gift of a class that could agree on one.

tech.name: The Greenhouse
tech.description: A white-framed glasshouse full of palms, ferns and orchids, kept warm all winter: the showpiece of a distinguished Environmental Science program.

tech.name: The Observatory
tech.description: A white dome that opens at night for a telescope, and an open evening every clear Friday: the showpiece of a distinguished Aerospace Engineering program.

tech.name: The Pond
tech.description: A big pond with reeds round its edge, lily pads, a wooden footbridge over the narrow end and a family of ducks who think it is theirs.

tech.name: The Arts Center
tech.description: A concert hall, two theaters and the studios behind them, under one roof and open late: the building the town comes to the college for, and the home of the MFA. Opens from Year 10, once every Arts & Media course is taught.

tech.name: The Research Park
tech.description: Laboratories at the edge of campus where faculty and industry work side by side: home of the Landmark Programs. Opens once the college is specialized in research.

tech.name: The Graduate College
tech.description: A quadrangle of its own for graduate students, with a hall to dine in and a tower to be seen from: the home of the six doctorates. Opens from Year 15, once any school's undergraduate courses are all taught.

tech.name: The Law School
tech.description: A courthouse of a building, with a moot court, a law library and a portico to argue under: the home of the School of Law. Opens from Year 15, once every Social Sciences & Humanities course is taught.

tech.name: The Graduate Business School
tech.description: Glass, a trading floor and an atrium where recruiters wait: the home of the MBA. Opens from Year 15, once every Business course is taught.

tech.name: The Faculty Training Institute
tech.description: Seminar rooms, a teaching studio with cameras at the back and a faculty lounge where old hands talk shop with new ones. Each year it takes professors for a term, and they come back one band better in the classroom. Opens once the college is specialized in academics.

tech.name: The Athletic Performance Complex
tech.description: A training center beside the venues: an indoor sprint straight under a sawtooth roof, a strength hall, a sports-science lab, recovery pools, film rooms and a speed field outside, where every varsity athlete trains. Opens once the college is specialized in athletics.

tech.name: The University Museum
tech.description: Decades of gifts, loans and bequests finally in one place and on show: a museum that schoolchildren are taken to and graduates bring their own children back to. Opens from Year 40, or Year 35 for a college at prestige 100.

tech.name: The Campanile
tech.description: A bell tower taller than anything for miles: the college on every postcard, and a clock the town sets its watches by.

tech.name: The Great Dome
tech.description: A domed rotunda over a great hall, the kind of room people travel to stand in.

tech.name: The Triumphal Gate
tech.description: An arch at the head of the campus with the college's name cut across it: the way every graduate walks out.
